data.text/markdown:
Occupancy grid mapping from laser scans

This notebook uses the MRPT Python wheel (pip install mrpt3) to build an occupancy grid map of a simulated office from the 2D laser scans of a robot whose path is known. It uses three MRPT modules:
  • mrpt.obs: the laser scan observation (CObservation2DRangeScan).
  • mrpt.poses: the robot pose at each scan (CPose3D).
  • mrpt.maps: the occupancy grid (COccupancyGridMap2D), updated with insertObservation().
An occupancy grid divides the floor into square cells, each one storing the probability of being occupied by an obstacle. Every laser ray is evidence that the cells it crosses are free, and that the cell where it ends is occupied. Move the sliders to insert more scans, add range noise, or change the cell size.

data.text/markdown:
1. Simulated laser scans

A CObservation2DRangeScan stores one range per ray, a validity flag per ray (no echo within maxRange means invalid), and the scan geometry: aperture (here 360°), rightToLeft and the sensor pose on the robot. The ranges come from ray-casting against the office walls, plus Gaussian noise.

2. Inserting the scans into the grid

insertObservation(scan, robot_pose) updates every cell touched by the rays of the scan, taken from the given robot pose. Each cell keeps its occupancy probability as log-odds, so a Bayesian update is just an addition: consistent observations accumulate, contradicting ones cancel out. getAsNumpy() returns the map as an image (1: free, 0: occupied, 0.5: never observed).
Grid of 280 × 200 cells of 10 cm. Observed so far: 85% of the building floor.

3. How a cell becomes certain

Each scan can change a cell only up to a maximum certainty (65% by default), so a cell needs several consistent observations to become confidently free or occupied. Below, the occupancy probability of the three cells circled in the map, as scans are inserted. Cells never reached by any ray, like the inside of furniture, stay at 0.5 (unknown).

Run it on your computer (Linux, Python 3.11 to 3.14): 
uvx marimo edit --sandbox https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MRPT/mrpt-notebooks/main/notebooks/occupancy_grid_mapping.py
More MRPT Python examples: mrpt_examples_py.
